meta.regime: A soft dollar sits at the centre of the tape after a run of dollar-negative catalysts. (1) The FOMC held 9-3 at 3.50-3.75% Jul 29 with three members dissenting FOR a hike and Chair Warsh refusing forward guidance; the market read it as a loss of anchor - 30-year yields spiked to ~5.23% (a 19-year high), inflation expectations rose, the dollar slid and equities fell. (2) US Q2 GDP then printed soft at 1.5% (advance, down from 2.1% in Q1), reinforcing the slide. (3) The BoE held 3.75% but on a 6-3 vote with three hike dissents - a hawkish hold that firms sterling. (4) On oil, WTI holds ~$84 and the Strait of Hormuz stays effectively closed (<14 ships/day vs ~120), but after nearly two weeks of exchanged strikes Trump says the US halted its attacks at Iran's request pending a new ceasefire - the premium is intact yet the escalation may be pausing, so headline risk is now two-way. Net regime: soft dollar, still-bid oil and havens (gold + franc), a real CAD terms-of-trade bid, hawkish-hold GBP, and high-beta AUD pressured by risk. Next gate: BoJ tomorrow.
meta.nextBigEvent: BoJ decision + updated forecasts (Fri Jul 31, 03:00Z): expected hold at 1.00% with GDP upgraded to 0.8% and a slow-hike bias (Oct/Dec debated). dailyRead: Both of today's gates cleared and both point the same way - a softer dollar and a firmer sterling. The BoE held Bank Rate at 3.75% as expected, but the vote was 6-3: a THIRD member joined Greene and Pill in dissenting for a hike as lingering energy-price pressure worried the hawks, even as June CPI cooled to 2.6%. That is a hawkish hold, and with the dollar already sliding it lifts cable - GBP/USD flips from RANGE to LONG. Minutes earlier, US Q2 GDP printed soft at 1.5% (advance, down from 2.1% in Q1, in line with the Atlanta Fed's 1.5% nowcast), a growth deceleration that deepens the post-Fed dollar slide. That Fed hold on Jul 29 was itself dollar-negative despite three hawkish dissents: Warsh gave no guidance, 30-year yields ripped to ~5.23% (a 19-year high) and the dollar fell - higher long yields with a weaker dollar is a credibility/fiscal-dominance tell. On the geopolitical leg, the picture is more two-way than yesterday: WTI still holds ~$84 (+6% on the week) and the Strait of Hormuz stays choked to under 14 ships a day, but after nearly two weeks of exchanged strikes Trump now says the US paused its attacks at Iran's request pending a new ceasefire. The risk premium is intact but the escalation may be cooling, so the oil and haven longs must be sized for a de-escalation snap-back. Cleanest expressions: EUR/USD LONG and GBP/USD LONG on the soft dollar (GBP with the added hawkish-hold kicker); USD/CHF SHORT and USD/CAD SHORT on the soft dollar plus, respectively, the live haven bid and a real oil bid; XAU/USD LONG (~$4,080) and XAG LONG (~$57.8, GSR ~70) on the slid dollar, higher inflation expectations and the haven flow; USOIL LONG but sized small given the fragile pause. Antipodeans: AUD/NZD SHORT still works - the soft AU Q2 trim (3.6% miss) deflated the RBA hike tail while NZD's 4.1% Q2 beat plus firm crude keep its petrol-CPI engine hot. Yen: weakest by spot ~163.7, but the dollar slide and a thin-Friday MoF intervention threat cap the weakness into BoJ tomorrow, so USD/JPY is a short-tilt RANGE. The one caveat over the whole book: a credible Iran de-escalation headline snaps the oil/haven premium back in a session.

geopolitics: The oil risk premium is intact but the war may be pausing - a two-way tape rather than one-way escalation. After nearly two weeks of exchanged strikes (CENTCOM hit hundreds of Iranian targets, including Bandar Abbas and IRGC/maritime sites, and Iran struck commercial vessels), Trump now says the US halted its attacks at Iran's request pending a new ceasefire, while Iran says there are no current negotiations. So the situation is fragile: WTI still holds ~$84 (Brent ~$89) and the Strait of Hormuz stays effectively closed - fewer than 14 ships in the last 24 hours versus a pre-war ~120, convoys under naval escort - which keeps the premium on the tape, but a confirmed de-escalation OR a resumption of strikes is now the swing factor. FX transmission: (1) CAD keeps a terms-of-trade bid while oil holds up - USD/CAD SHORT (soft dollar + firm oil), though CAD is still domestically soft. (2) CHF's haven bid stays live while the strait is shut - USD/CHF SHORT, CHF the cleaner haven versus the energy-importing yen, but slightly less one-way given the pause talk. (3) Gold and silver are bid on the slid dollar, higher inflation expectations and the haven flow (~$4,080 / ~$57.8) - XAU/XAG LONG. (4) The JPY loses ground as an oil importer but the dollar slide and MoF intervention risk cap its weakness - USD/JPY short-tilt RANGE. (5) High-beta AUD is the antipodean risk aversion hurts most; NZD is cushioned because firm crude sustains its petrol-CPI engine. (6) USOIL stays LONG but conviction is trimmed to LOW-MED because a credible de-escalation headline snaps the premium back in a session - size for two-way headline risk.
